_about: Client profile and screening rules for the residency filter. Change what the filter looks for here. Nothing in the Python needs touching.

client.practice: Mixed media, sculpture and installation, trained in typography.
client.style: Dramatic, surrealist and figurative: containment and vitrines, the body breaking the picture plane, hyperrealism used for unease, scale distortion, a restrained palette with one loud accent, the senses as subject.
client._years_note: Years of professional practice since graduating. Unknown for now. Fill in to settle residencies with an experience minimum, such as TOKAS at 5 years.

hard_gates._about: A residency failing any gate is disqualified outright. Set a gate to false to relax it. An UNKNOWN value never fails a gate, it sends the residency to the verify list instead.
hard_gates._fee_note: Andrea, 2026-09-23, restated in full and this supersedes the earlier INR 5000 allowance: 'If there's an application fee, I want you to skip that.' ANY application fee disqualifies, EUR 10 as much as USD 65. The one exception is a fee the host explicitly waives for his named category, quoted from the host's own page, such as Skowhegan waiving its USD 25 for Indian artists under 35 living in India; a discretionary, needs-based or on-request waiver does not count. A cost to stay is separate from an application fee and is capped at INR 5000 per week. Incidental costs he would pay anywhere, his own flights, materials, visa and insurance, are recorded but never disqualify.
hard_gates._rules_note: Andrea's rules, 2026-09-23. Funding is no longer required: free to apply plus a place to work is enough, and free accommodation is a bonus. ANY application fee disqualifies, however small. The residency must be outside India. Digital art is welcome, so digital-only programmes no longer disqualify. A programme locked to one material or craft, such as ceramics, pottery, glass or furniture, disqualifies, because the practice is mixed media.

weights._about: Points out of 100 for residencies that pass every gate.

style_keywords._about: Matched against what the residency says about itself, never against research notes. Keywords match as word prefixes; a trailing $ means whole word only. A residency record can override this with style_fit (0 to 1) plus style_fit_reason.
style_keywords._negative_note: Digital, new media and AI were removed on 2026-09-23: Andrea confirmed the artist is open to digital art. What remains negative is a programme narrowed to one craft or discipline that is not his, or to a non-visual art form.

country_practicality._about: Starting heuristic for an Indian passport holder, 0 to 1. Weighs visa friction, travel from India, and cost of living against a typical stipend. Edit freely. Visa rules change often, so confirm with the embassy before applying.

_default.why: Country not in the table. Check visa and cost manually.

India.why: Home country. No visa, lowest cost.

Nepal.why: No visa needed for Indian nationals, short travel.

Bhutan.why: Low entry friction for Indian nationals, short travel.

Thailand.why: Short flight from India, generally low visa friction.

Singapore.why: Short flight and routine visa process, but high cost of living.

Japan.why: Visa needed but routine with an invitation letter. Direct flights from India. High cost of living, so check the stipend covers it.

South Korea.why: Visa needed, generally manageable with an invitation.

Taiwan.why: Visa needed, generally manageable with an invitation.

United Kingdom.why: Visa needed and relatively costly. Well-trodden route from India with many direct flights. London is expensive.

France.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter, but appointment waits can be long in peak season.

Italy.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter, but appointment waits can be long in peak season.

Switzerland.why: Schengen visa needed, and very high cost of living against most stipends.

Finland.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter.

Sweden.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter.

Norway.why: Schengen visa needed, and high cost of living.

Denmark.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter.

Greece.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter.

Poland.why: Schengen visa needed. Manageable with an invitation letter, lower cost of living.

Ireland.why: Separate Irish visa needed, not covered by a Schengen or UK visa.

Australia.why: Visa needed, long and costly flight.

Canada.why: Visa needed. Processing times for Indian applicants have often been long, so start early.

United States.why: Visa needed. Interview waits in India have often been very long, and paid residencies can raise visa-category questions.
